q1.prompt: User 42 writes comment 91 to the primary, then immediately reads from an async replica lagging 200 ms. What can happen?

choices.label: The read can miss comment 91 even though the write returned success
The replica must contain the comment because all replicas are instantly current

wrong1.prompt: Asynchronous replicas can serve stale data.
wrong1.explanation: The primary can acknowledge before a replica replays the commit. Replication lag changes what an immediate read may observe.

q2.prompt: How can the product provide read-your-writes for that user without routing every reader to the primary forever?

choices.label: Temporarily pin the user or require a replica caught up to the write position
Pick any replica randomly and assume the lag is harmless

wrong2.explanation: A session can carry the commit position or use temporary primary affinity. Other users whose reads tolerate lag may still use replicas normally.

q3.prompt: The primary fails before its last async commits reach a replica. What must failover acknowledge?

choices.label: Possible loss of acknowledged writes, plus fencing the old primary before promotion
Zero loss is guaranteed and the old primary may keep accepting writes

wrong3.prompt: Async failover has an RPO and split-brain risk.
wrong3.explanation: An async replica may not have the newest commits. Fencing prevents two writers when the old primary returns.

success.prompt: You connected replica lag to user-visible consistency and made failover guarantees honest.
